name: save-load-visual
description: Visual verification of the save/load UI: multiple save slots, auto-save indicator, save/load buttons, export/import options, slot metadata display (date, level, cash, playtime), and IndexedDB backend for web persistence.

steps.description: #553: was `campaign start level:dusty_hollow` -- a manually-bought vehicle spawns at grid centre (FleetPanel/vehicle.ts), and dusty_hollow's 96x40x96 campaign grid put that centre dozens of tiles from this file's own drill site (15,15), the same terrain-reachability trap found and worked around in scores-display-visual.json. Switched to new_game's flat 64x64x64 default (no obstruction) and bumped cash from $50,000 to $120,000 -- this file now needs a driller/drill_rig it never used to, on top of the original save/load-only shopping list.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed any roster at all) now needs one first. Employee #1.

Grants the driller (employee #1) the licence to drive the drill_rig just purchased -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow); left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is save/load, not re-proving vehicle licensing.

expect.note: #553: no longer flat -- the driller/drill_rig now on the roster drain payroll/maintenance even while idle, unlike the pre-#553 empty roster this file used to open with.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Left unmarked: "quicksave" isn't a real UI slot -- SavesModal.ts only exposes 'auto' and numbered 'slot_N' (SAVE_SLOT_COUNT) slots. The real UI flow is demonstrated for real below (steps 10/11/16, clicking #bs-saveload-btn and a numbered slot), just under a different slot name than this console-only quicksave.
Open the Save/Load panel (multiple slots, auto-save row, export/import, slot metadata) via its top-bar button.

SavesModal.ts's saveToSlot() re-renders the slot list but never calls hide() (unlike loadFromSlot(), which does) -- the modal stays open after a save and its .bs-confirm-overlay tier covers the toolbar underneath, blocking the next step's click. Closes it explicitly via the header's close button.

expect.note: the real UI slot_1 here goes through SavesModal.ts's own IndexedDB-backed persistence -- a completely separate backend from the console save/load commands' in-memory quickSaveSlots map used above. This is the actual save the later load step reads back.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Drill a small plan after slot 1 was saved, so the blast below craters terrain the saved slot does not know about. depth corrected from 4 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: drill_plan now only orders holes -- holeCount stays 0 until the driller actually drives the drill_rig to each one and drills it, proven by the wait step below. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission kept the drill_rig busy (fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks command mode never should have spent, a $48 divergence at the charge step below. Confirmed exact: adding the real default reproduces interaction mode's own $77,994 figure precisely.
#553: waits for the driller to drive the drill_rig to all 4 ordered holes and drill them (sandbox-measured: lands around tick 70 on new_game's flat default terrain, well inside this single round).
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.
Blast a crater into the live scene after slot 1's save, so the load step below must actually regenerate terrain (not just leave the cratered grid on screen) to prove itself.

Load back slot 1 by clicking the Saves modal's own Load button (SavesModal.ts, main.ts's setOnLoad handler) — not a raw console command — so this step exercises the click-driven path that must regenerate the grid, replacing the post-blast crater above with clean terrain matching the saved state. The command field stays the inert `state` read (rather than `load slot:...`) so command mode does not pre-clear the crater itself and mask a regression in the click path.

expect.note: #553: cash dropped from this check -- command mode's own command field is the inert `state` read (see this step's description), so it never actually reverts anything and reports whatever cash the post-blast state already holds. Before #553 that coincidentally equalled the pre-save value too, because nothing in this file ever spent cash; now that the driller/drill_rig genuinely drain payroll over the drilling wait, post-blast cash and the saved slot's cash have diverged for real, so cash is no longer safely checkable across both modes (same class as Findings #21/#22/#31). holeCount stays checkable: it is 0 in both paths for the same reason as before (post-blast always zeroes it; the saved slot never had any holes ordered yet either). In a real browser, the click genuinely reverts cash to slot_1's pre-blast save -- only interaction mode is actually testing the load; the terrain/voxel revert this step's whole point is about has no state field to check at all, only the screenshot.

#553: cash/tickCount dropped from this check for the same cross-mode-divergence reason as the load step above -- command mode never actually reverts, so both now read whatever the post-blast state holds (cash 79226, tickCount 90ish) rather than the saved slot's own values (cash 82720, tickCount 20). holeCount stays checkable since it is 0 either way.
